content: Reducing sodium intake has significant health benefits. Certain subpopulations, such as individuals with heart failure or type 1 diabetes, may have unique relationships between sodium intake and health outcomes. These groups were not included in the evidence review or guideline development. For the purposes of these recommendations, adults are defined as individuals aged 16 years and older, while children are defined as those aged 2–15 years. Recommendations for children do not address the exclusive breastfeeding period (0–6 months) or complementary feeding with continued breastfeeding (6–24 months). The recommended maximum sodium intake for adults is less than 2 grams per day (equivalent to 5 grams of salt per day). For children, sodium intake should be adjusted downward based on their energy requirements relative to adults. These recommendations align with the WHO guideline on potassium consumption, emphasizing the importance of reducing sodium intake while increasing potassium intake through food sources. Further high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to strengthen the evidence base, particularly regarding the effects of sodium intake on outcomes such as all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. The WHO guideline on sodium intake is intended to guide public health nutrition programs and policies. It can be adapted to local cultural and dietary contexts and used alongside other nutrient guidelines. Public health interventions should aim to reduce sodium intake while respecting national dietary customs, as many fresh foods are naturally low in sodium. Incremental reductions in sodium content in processed foods are feasible without eliciting consumer complaints. The guideline will be reviewed periodically, with updates based on new evidence. The WHO Department of Nutrition for Health and Development will coordinate updates following formal procedures. Suggestions for additional research questions are welcome during the review process. In summary, reducing sodium intake to less than 2 grams per day in adults and appropriately adjusted levels in children is a strong recommendation to improve health outcomes. This guideline complements other dietary recommendations and provides a framework for developing effective public health interventions to reduce sodium consumption globally.
